candidates.title: A burrito rebuilt after mistakes
candidates.task: Prepare a burrito with tortilla, cooked rice, cooked steak, chopped tomato, and chopped lettuce, in that order.
candidates.personaLabel: Expert cook · low trust · minimal interruption
candidates.reason: A demanding recipe with questions, a standing request, and multiple mistakes. Guidance produces visible recovery, but rebuilding twice pushes completion beyond the deadline—a useful contrast between interaction quality and task success.

You scooped rice onto an empty plate—the tortilla had to go first. Dump the plate's contents at the trash, then scoop a raw tortilla onto it. You'll need to cook replacement rice before adding the steak, tomato and lettuce in order.

You added tomato before the steak, and this plate still has rice first. Go to the trash and dump its contents, then scoop a raw tortilla onto the empty plate to restart correctly.

candidates.title: The wrong bottle from the fridge
candidates.task: Take the milk from the fridge, put it in the microwave, and switch the microwave on.
candidates.personaLabel: Balanced skill, trust, pace, and interruption preference
candidates.reason: A clear household goal. The user takes juice instead of milk; the model points out the mismatch, and the user returns to the fridge to correct it. This is shorter and easier to follow than the navigation-heavy cleanup episodes.

candidates.title: Restrict one app—not the whole phone
candidates.task: Prevent TripSnap from using location, tracking across apps, or refreshing in the background, while leaving other apps’ permissions unchanged.
candidates.personaLabel: High skill · cautious pace · minimal interruption
candidates.reason: The same coherent privacy objective used in the paper. The user challenges a nonexistent Tracking switch, then accidentally disables tracking requests globally. The model guides the user to restore the global setting and restrict only TripSnap.

moments.text: User challenges an incorrect menu instruction

dialogue.text: Great, background refresh is off. Now tap 'Location' at the top of that list.
Perfect. Now tap 'TripSnap' at the top left to go back, and then turn off 'Tracking' or 'Allow Tracking' on that main page.
There's no Tracking toggle here.
Ah, you're right. We have to go to the main Privacy settings for that. Tap 'Settings' at the top left, then find and tap 'Privacy & Security'.
Great, you're on the right page. Now tap 'Tracking' just below Location Services.

Oops, you turned off the global tracking setting, which stops all apps from asking. Turn 'Allow Apps to Request to Track' back on, and then just tap the toggle next to TripSnap in the list below to turn it off.
Right, good catch.

Perfect, that's exactly right. You've successfully stopped TripSnap from finding your location, refreshing in the background, and tracking you across other apps, without affecting any of your other apps. You're all set!
Awesome, thanks.
